quotes.text: # Accept a payment using local cards in Nigeria
This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:

old_evidence.text: Integrating with Naira card enables Nigerian customers to pay using Nigerian-issued cards.
The minimum amount accepted is 500 NGN, and the maximum amount accepted is 100,000,000 NGN.
Listen for these events rather than waiting on a callback from the client.

findings: November retains the local card acceptance identity and supplies the Checkout and Direct API links, which are the two full May variants (new raw lines 5-12, old raw lines 4-14,105-113). Neither an implementation change nor a withdrawal of May behavior is established.

Existing source lines 18-28 and Nigeria concept lines 44-49 compress the May Checkout compatibility and selection branches. Distinguish US business, Nigerian customers and Nigerian-issued cards, NGN presentment, the Checkout-specific 500–100,000,000 NGN bounds and all NGN line items. With dynamic methods Stripe evaluates applicability, and explicit `ng_card` listing is the manual path. Compatibility lists payment/setup/subscription, but the hosted `success_url` and embedded `return_url`/`ui_mode: 'embedded_page'` examples both use payment mode (old raw lines 8-46,48-103).

Source line 32 and Nigeria concept line 49 make the May create example read as a universal double-field rule. Old raw lines 128-148 describe server creation with amount, currency `ngn` and `ng_card` in `payment_method_types`; the example also supplies `payment_method_data.type` there. Old raw lines 241-259 show the same type again on client confirmation with the intent secret and return URL. Preserve the exact sample placement without turning it into a general schema requirement. May error handling destructures `error` yet accesses undeclared `result.error.message` (old raw lines 250-265).

Source lines 35-37 and Nigeria concept lines 50-52 need an explicit state boundary. The local merchant-of-record provider handles customer authentication and authorization, and Stripe redirects back with `payment_intent` and `payment_intent_client_secret` for status lookup. The May guide advises asynchronous `payment_intent.succeeded` handling through Dashboard, a webhook or partner integration for post-payment actions. The test transitions `requires_action` → `succeeded` or `requires_payment_method` are sandbox-only (old raw lines 109-113,241-284). Return alone establishes neither success nor balance, fulfillment or payout.

The separate November Nigeria family overview describes an invitation request, the Nigerian partner as merchant of record and US accounts with USD settlement, alongside NGN presentment (raw/stripe-payments-countries-nigeria-2026-11-07.md:7-15,27-42,63-90). Retain those separate evidence scopes if routing readers to the broader context. Invitation request or front-end display gives no access approval. The May bank-transfer acceptance guide specifically excludes Checkout setup/subscription while the card guide lists them (raw/stripe-ng-bank-transfer-accept-payment-2025.md:16-44 and old raw lines 20-37). The separate November family matrix lists card recurring Yes and transfer recurring No (same November country raw lines 109-117).

source_assessments.reason: Navigation-only capture replacement. Independently repair May summary scope for manual listing, server field examples and payment verification, including the reciprocal concept route.

answers.Q1: The November 7 capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payments/ng-card/accept-a-payment identifies acceptance of locally issued Nigerian cards and links Checkout and Direct API (new raw lines 5-12). The May 8 guide describes Nigerian customers using Nigerian-issued cards, US merchants, NGN presentment and Checkout limits of 500–100,000,000 NGN, with all Checkout line items in NGN. It lists compatibility for payment, setup and subscription modes and shows payment-only examples for hosted Checkout with success_url and embedded Checkout with return_url and ui_mode=embedded_page. Stripe evaluates eligible dynamic methods, while manual selection lists ng_card (old raw lines 8-46 and old raw lines 48-103). In Direct API, the server creates a PaymentIntent and passes the client secret. The browser calls stripe.confirmPayment with a return URL, the local merchant-of-record provider handles authentication and authorization, and Stripe returns PaymentIntent identifiers for a status lookup. The Direct API sandbox example transitions from requires_action to succeeded on simulated authorization or to requires_payment_method on simulated failure. The post-payment guidance recommends listening for payment_intent.succeeded rather than relying on a browser callback (old raw lines 105-153 and old raw lines 222-296). source-stripe-ng-card-accept-payment.md preserves the principal May flow but needs separate treatment of manual listing, create-time example fields and status verification.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/ng-card/accept-a-payment, new raw lines 5-12 retain the guide's identity and replace the May Checkout and Direct API bodies with navigation. The November family overview separately shows a Nigerian partner merchant-of-record arrangement, US accounts with USD settlement and an invitation request, which neither validates account approval nor changes the acceptance index's evidence scope. Keep the May 8, 2026 NGN and amount restrictions, supported Checkout modes, hosted and embedded payment samples and test descriptions dated (old raw lines 2-46 and old raw lines 48-103). The reciprocal Nigeria concept and source-stripe-ng-card-accept-payment.md should distinguish dynamic selection from manual listing, the server example's payment_method_data from prose requirements, the historical Dahlia and confirmation snippet, and the server-to-client PaymentIntent secret handoff (old raw lines 128-189 and old raw lines 222-267). Preserve the dated callback example's error-handler mismatch. Authentication or a return URL does not verify outcome. Sandbox transitions do not prove live payment, and a live PaymentIntent's succeeded status concerns payment completion without establishing merchant payout (old raw lines 269-296).
